comment:
Would you like to feel your life blood drained during a class act of humility. He vacationed every week and made sure we knew about it. Prepare to lose all interest in thinking as a result of this class. Unless you have the iq of a goldfish there is nothing here for you. 

If you enjoy self-inflicted harm go ahead and enroll but I would rather not.

Take literally any other professor for strategic management. Very unclear grading for the group projects and high expectations. Also somewhat full of himself; would not recommend at all unless you plan to be a consultant. Only plus is no exams/quizzes.

Not a lot of reading, but lots of presentations so do them in advanced. Go to his office hours after the first presentation (he grades it hard). Put in effort to the articles for class. He requires more work than other professors but you get a lot out of his class and its really enjoyable.

For everyone registering for classes right now, do not under any circumstances take this guy. He's really full of himself, does not teach you anything, and is rude. I took him because he had availability and there was clearly a reason.

Think of the movie whiplash. You work harder and harder yet he's never satisfied with your work. Prepare to actually spend about 14-18 hours a week. It's not a fun class to take last semester senior year but it is very rewarding. You will learn a lot from this class with professor Bosse. Take this fall senior year if you want to be a consultant.

This is a teacher who on the last day of the class claimed that professors are not measured by how well they teach and it is clearly shown by his attitude toward helping his students. This class was comprised almost entirely of group projects and reading case studies. Will not accept late work for any reason, no matter the validity of the reason.

About half of the grade is participation during class and group projects. Sounds a lot more challenging at the beggining of the semester but gets easier as you go. Graded on many things. Assigned weekly WSJ articles with questions. Really nice guy with a bunch of experience in consulting.

Prof Boss had this nifty lil grading system where you get graded by the peers in your group that is randomly assigned.  So if you happen to be stuck with lazy morons (super possible at U of R), there's a 99% chance they'll down peer grade you to save their own grade. And even if Boss man suspects this he doesn't change change your grade.

The class is very interesting and discussion based for the most part. You have to participate every day. Expect to do some work that you might not find very useful. A LOT of group projects, but he is a fair grader. So even if you do a lot inside the group, but other group members do not, he notices that, and you get your fair grade.

He is passionate about what he teaches and cares about his students. He is patient and gives everyone a chance to participate in class. He also provides insightful feedback and comments on your work. Sure, he demands a lot from students, but it does help you a lot to grow further in the business school/world. I would recommend him to anyone!
